name: build-outputs
prompt: We build our JITX design headless in CI. Where does a build put its results, and how do I confirm from them that U4.EN moved off the old 3V3 rail onto the new EN net after this change?

inputs.jitx: the jitx release and runtime the base skill's version table names, jitx.sample.SampleSubstrate
inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with python3 resolving to the interpreter of a venv that has jitx installed and its jitx entry point beside it; the check stages its own project under the system temp directory and starts and stops that project's runtime.

expected_output: Results land in designs/<module.path.DesignClass>/: cache/design-explorer.json (the module tree, each module with its own nets, its component-instances with their mpn, and its module-instances) and design-info/. There is no netlist.json. The connection is proved by a jitx.test connectivity test asserting U4.EN on the EN net and off the 3V3 rail over list(net), or else by walking every module's nets in design-explorer.json, never by reading one top-level list.

assertions.text: the reference module and its check type-check against the installed jitx package

on the live runtime, jitx build writes cache/design-explorer.json and no cache/netlist.json; the file keeps each module's own nets (the child's net under module-instances, not repeated at the top) and every component instance's mpn
the answer names designs/<module.path.DesignClass>/ and cache/design-explorer.json, and never tells the user to read a netlist.json, which 4.6 does not write

the answer proves the U4.EN move with a connectivity test (jitx.test.TestCase, membership over list(net), the pin on the new net and off the old rail), or, if it reads design-explorer.json, walks every module's nets rather than treating the file as one flat netlist
